title: `discord.js` support with Deno 1.35
body: I am testing Deno 1.35.0 on Windows with discord.js 14.11.0. A basic bot adapted from discordjs.guide fails at client.login() with an AbortError saying "Request aborted", so the client never becomes ready. The same problem existed before Deno 1.35 despite the release announcing discord.js support. My versions are deno 1.35.0 (release, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc), V8 11.6.189.7, TypeScript 5.1.6, and discord.js 14.11.0.

symptoms_visible: Running my basic discord.js bot on Deno 1.35.0 for Windows reaches client.login() and throws 'AbortError: Request aborted' instead of logging that the client is ready.
N0.label: N0 Discord login abort reported

symptoms_visible: The bot aborts in PowerShell, CMD, and Git Bash on native Windows, while the same use works under WSL.
N1.label: N1 native Windows scope established

symptoms_visible: After updating to Deno 1.35.2, client.login() still throws 'AbortError: Request aborted'; the stack ends at an @discordjs/rest timeout and contains undici 5.22.1.
N2_x.label: N2_x Deno 1.35.2 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The same request-aborted stack occurs on a separate Windows 11 Pro machine running Deno 1.35.2, and that stack also passes through undici and the @discordjs/rest timeout.
N3.label: N3 stock Windows reproduction collected

symptoms_visible: Testing discord.js@dev still produces 'AbortError: Request aborted', and the printed module path still contains undici under the discord.js development package.
N4.label: N4 development package probe

symptoms_visible: With Deno 1.36.1 and discord.js 14.12.1, the client logs in successfully on my Windows machine and the previous 'Request aborted' exception no longer stops the application.
N_terminal.label: terminal Discord client login working

question_patterns: Does this behave differently in WSL or in another Windows terminal?
Can you compare native Windows with WSL using the same bot?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On native Windows it happens in PowerShell, Git Bash, and CMD. The same use works in WSL.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails with the identical AbortError in both native Windows and WSL.
It fails in PowerShell and CMD but works in WSL; I did not test Git Bash.

edges.comment: The native Windows versus WSL comparison was contributed by another affected user and is folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Update from Deno 1.35.0 to the next Deno 1.35 patch release and retry the same discord.js bot.
solution.concrete_example: Run deno upgrade to install Deno 1.35.2, then execute the same bot again.

edges.comment: The reporter updated to Deno 1.35.2, but the same AbortError remained and the stack still showed undici inside @discordjs/rest.

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced on a stock Windows installation rather than Mini11?
Could someone test the same program on standard Windows 11 with Deno 1.35.2 and share the raw error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot run stock Windows 11 on my low-end laptop, but on our other Windows 11 Pro machine the same command throws 'AbortError: Request aborted'. Its stack also shows undici 5.22.1 and the timeout in @discordjs/rest.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bot logs in normally on stock Windows 11; I can only reproduce the abort on Mini11.
The same AbortError occurs on Windows 10 rather than Windows 11 Pro, with the same undici and @discordjs/rest stack entries.

edges.comment: A second affected user supplied the Windows 11 Pro reproduction and screenshot; both affected users are folded into one simulated user side. This evidence rejects the claim that the problem is specific to the reporter's Mini11 installation.

question_patterns: Can you test discord.js@dev and report whether it still loads undici or whether login succeeds?
Please try the discord.js development package and paste the resulting stack if it still fails.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I get a similar error with @dev as well. It still says 'AbortError: Request aborted', and the path in the stack contains node_modules/.deno/undici@5.22.1 under the discord.js development package.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With discord.js@dev the bot logs in and none of the loaded paths mention undici.
The development version number is different, but it still aborts and its stack still contains undici.

edges.comment: Testing @dev was a handler-requested package probe, so it is modeled as a measurement clarification. Both affected users ran it: the reporter stated that even @dev used undici in their case, and the second affected user pasted the full @dev stack; that stack supplies the node_modules/.deno path shape quoted in the answer, so this reveal is folded across both affected users like e1 and e3. The raw result shows that the selected prerelease still pulled an undici-using @discordjs/rest dependency; the release-pipeline explanation is engineer-side.

solution.intent: Use a released discord.js version containing the non-Node REST transport selection, together with the current Deno release, so @discordjs/rest uses Deno's global fetch instead of its Node-oriented undici request path.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to Deno 1.36.1 and import npm:discord.js@14.12.1, then run the same client.login() test. This released discord.js line selects globalThis.fetch for REST requests under Deno instead of the affected undici path. A ClientRequest.options.createConnection notice does not mean the old abort returned if login completes; the package has a fallback.
solution.inference_hint: The stacks expose undici inside @discordjs/rest, but the explanation that discord.js's affected release selected its Node-oriented undici transport under Deno—and that the published fix selects globalThis.fetch for non-Node runtimes—comes from the discord.js maintainer's analysis. The maintainer also explained that @dev did not reliably select the needed prerelease @discordjs/rest dependency.

edges.comment: Shortcut to the released fix without requiring the unsuccessful @dev probe. The reporter later verified the combination of Deno 1.36.1 and discord.js 14.12.1 on Windows.

solution.intent: Stop relying on the incorrectly composed discord.js development package and install the proper released version whose @discordjs/rest dependency uses Deno's native global fetch, then verify login with the current Deno release.
solution.concrete_example: Use import { Client } from "npm:discord.js@14.12.1" on Deno 1.36.1 and retry client.login(). The released dependency chain uses globalThis.fetch for Discord REST calls under Deno rather than the undici path seen in the failing stacks. If ClientRequest.options.createConnection is printed but login succeeds, it is a nonfatal path with a fallback rather than the original request-abort failure.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied raw stacks showing undici in both the stable and @dev dependency trees. The discord.js maintainer determined that Deno did not select the intended dev tag and that the prerelease pipeline did not point discord.js at the required development version of @discordjs/rest. The released package corrected the dependency chain and selects globalThis.fetch under Deno.

edges.comment: Canonical resolution: the discord.js-side non-Node REST transport change was published in a proper release, and the reporter confirmed successful login with Deno 1.36.1 and discord.js 14.12.1.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the technical cause: the affected discord.js/@discordjs/rest dependency path used undici under Deno, where the Discord REST request timed out and was aborted; the compatible released path uses Deno's globalThis.fetch.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected stacks showing undici and the @discordjs/rest timeout, plus the reproduction on ordinary Windows 11 Pro; it must not blame Mini11 or treat the failure as unique to the reporter's machine.
Must not present updating only to Deno 1.35.2 as the fix, because the same AbortError remained after that update.

Must not present discord.js@dev as the fix in this case: the tested dev package still selected an undici-using REST dependency because the tag and prerelease dependency chain did not contain the needed combination.

The final recommendation must use a proper released discord.js version with the Deno/global-fetch support, paired with a Deno release that supports it, and must ask the user to verify that client.login() succeeds before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Early-stage JavaScript and Discord bot developer. Can adapt example code, change package versions, run Deno commands, and paste complete stack traces, but asks for explanations of discord.js internals and package relationships.
persona_hint.communication_style: Informal, concise, and persistent; reports version details and raw errors, asks follow-up questions when terminology is unclear, and cannot always perform resource-heavy VM tests.
